The way the ordering system works (or at least used to work, I'd heard rumors that they changed it recently) was that you'd start with a basic burger. Every burger comes with spread/lettuce/tomato, then onions were offered as optional. If the customer wanted onions, there was a "W" button for "with". If the customer wanted no onions there was a "WO" button, for without. If the customer wanted no tomato, there was a "SL" button for "spread/lettuce". Those were the basic options. Then we had individual letters to represent each item if somebody wanted a burger other than the basic options. So if a person wanted a burger with only spread and onion you'd press the "S" for spread and "O" for onion, and then there was an "only" button, which was mostly there for the customers to see clearly that their order was "S O Only". Thus you'd start with a base burger, HMB, CHB, or DBL, and add the appropriate condiments. The only time you would indicate that a burger didn't have something was when you put in "WO".

So a double double with no tomato but with onion would look like this:

Dbl

SL O

Or if they wanted spread only:

Dbl

>S only

Then animal style was the opposite. If you ordered animal style but wanted to remove something you'd add its letter after the animal option. So an animal style double double with no tomato would read:

Dbl

>Animal T

Then if you wanted to add something on an animal style burger you'd add it the same way. So an animal style double with ketchup would be:

Dbl

>Animal K

Occasionally somebody would want a double double with no cheese though. We called that a double meat. This had its own button, as there was no "no cheese" button. So then a double meat with onion would read like this:

DblMt

W

Then if they wanted just one piece of cheese, we called that a double single. That was run through as a double meat, but you'd add extra cheese. So that would read something like this:

DblMt

W XCheese

So basically we never used buttons to remove something from an order, we'd only indicate what was actually on the burger. The exception of course being the animal style burger and in those cases it was done as indicated above. It was a really peculiar way of notating orders, but that's how we did it. You can feel free to verify this at any in n out location. It's only been recently that I'd heard they changed the ordering system, so even if they have I'm sure somebody would remember how it used to be done. I worked there 2009 - 2010.

Edit: Here is a receipt from 2013

Looking at the receipt, you can see kind of how it worked.

The first burger is a Double Double with no onions, but with Ketchup and Mustard. Also the ketchup and mustard are in addition to the spread because we had an "inst" button for when the ketchup and mustard was replacing the spread.

The second burger is a three by three (three meat / three cheese) with GRilled onions and Spread only.

Then the rest of the order is pretty much self explanatory.
